additions.reason: The Torah opens with 'עֵינַיִם הֵם דְּבָרִים עֶלְיוֹנִים וּגְבוֹהִים מְאֹד' — Eyes ARE lofty and exalted things. This is the dominant/central concept of the entire teaching. The eyes are described as always seeing great and wondrous things, implying they are instruments of spiritual perception. This is the primary bechina node of Package 1.
additions.source_quote: עֵינַיִם הֵם דְּבָרִים עֶלְיוֹנִים וּגְבוֹהִים מְאֹד, וְהֵם רוֹאִים תָּמִיד דְּבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים וְנוֹרָאִים

additions.reason: The eyes ARE lofty and exalted things — this is the predicate of the primary bechina statement. It represents the spiritual dimension/domain that eyes occupy: the realm of elevated spiritual realities.
additions.source_quote: עֵינַיִם הֵם דְּבָרִים עֶלְיוֹנִים וּגְבוֹהִים מְאֹד

additions.reason: Great and wondrous things are what the eyes continuously see — this is the content of spiritual vision. The text identifies these great things as visions and revelations (מראות וחזיונות), making this a bechina node equivalent to divine revelation.
additions.source_quote: וְהֵם רוֹאִים תָּמִיד דְּבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים וְנוֹרָאִים

additions.reason: The text uses the definitive parenthetical equivalence '(הַיְנוּ מַרְאוֹת וְחֶזְיוֹנוֹת)' to identify the great things the eyes see as visions and revelations. The word הַיְנוּ (i.e., meaning that is) is classic bechina language — declaring that one thing IS another.
additions.source_quote: וְכֵן הָאָדָם רוֹאֶה בְּעֵינָיו תָּמִיד דְּבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים (הַיְנוּ מַרְאוֹת וְחֶזְיוֹנוֹת)

additions.reason: Proper/worthy eyes (עינים כשרים) are the eyes in their ideal realized state — not a different faculty but the same spiritual instrument of the eyes functioning at its full potential. If one merited these, they would know great things just from what their eyes see. This is the eyes as they ought to be — a specification of the same essential node.
additions.source_quote: וְאִם הָיָה הָאָדָם זוֹכֶה לְעֵינַיִם כְּשֵׁרִים, הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ דְּבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים רַק מִמַּה שֶּׁעֵינָיו רוֹאוֹת

additions.reason: The power of sight (כח הראות) is the active force/faculty of the eyes. The text refers to it as the operative mechanism that must 'reach out' (יוֹשִׁיט) to the da'at to make the vision known. It is the same essential reality as the eyes named from the angle of their functional power.
additions.source_quote: יָבוֹא וְיוֹשִׁיט כֹּחַ הָרְאוּת לְהַדַּעַת אֶת הַדָּבָר הַנִּרְאֶה

additions.reason: Da'at (knowledge/consciousness/awareness) is the faculty through which seen things become known. The text makes a structural claim: 'לֵידַע הַדָּבָר שֶׁרָאָה זֶה תָּלוּי בַּדַּעַת' — knowing what one saw depends on/belongs to da'at. The relationship between vision and da'at is partially bechina (vision reaches/extends to da'at, suggesting they are different facets of the same cognitive reality) and partially eitza (vision must reach da'at for knowledge to occur). Given the ambiguity, da'at is flagged as a candidate node — potentially a neutral node since da'at appears across many domains in Likutey Moharan. The text does not use explicit 'הוא בחינת' language for da'at, but the structural dependency 'תָּלוּי בַּדַּעַת' suggests an essential connection.
additions.source_quote: כִּי לֵידַע הַדָּבָר שֶׁרָאָה זֶה תָּלוּי בַּדַּעַת

eitza_concepts_excluded_from_packages: מהירות (speed/swiftness) — this is the obstacle/cause that prevents vision from reaching da'at. It is an eitza relationship: speed PREVENTS the vision from reaching da'at. It does not share the same essential nature as the eyes/vision cluster; it is the opposing causal force.

זמן (time) — this is the condition needed for vision to reach da'at: 'צָרִיךְ קְצָת זְמַן שֶׁיַּשְׁהֶה קְצָת הַדָּבָר'. It is an eitza-condition, not a bechina equivalence. Time enables the process; it does not share the essential nature of the vision faculty.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_analysis: Torah #254 presents a short, descriptive teaching with no explicit evil dimension. The teaching describes a neutral spiritual reality (the eyes' nature and their relationship to da'at) rather than prescribing a path or naming an opposing force. There is no evil package mirror in this Torah — unlike many Likutey Moharan teachings, this one does not name an opposing force or klipah equivalent. The 'obstacle' is simply the natural condition of human speed and lack of time, not a named evil force.
analysis_notes.note_on_torah_length: Torah #254 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutey Moharan Volume 1 — only 3 sentences. Its conceptual vocabulary is correspondingly limited. The teaching makes two key bechina claims: (1) eyes ARE lofty spiritual realities, and (2) the great things they see ARE visions and revelations. The remainder is analogy and explanation.
